## Observed

`classifyItem` (src/generator.ts, shipped in 2026.11.10) is documented as a two-tier classifier. Type and tags are trusted; the title is consulted only as a fallback, because descriptive prose collides with command and file names. The `Security` and `Deprecated` checks break that rule. Both run first, against `allValues` (type + tags + title), so any title that merely names something containing `security` lands under **Security**, ahead of every strong-tier signal.

Reproduced in unbraind/pm-cli while regenerating the changelog on 2026-11-11. A `Task` tagged `artifact,npm,package-size,release` and titled *"Exclude the repository-specific dependency-security and algorithm-portfolio docs from the npm tarball to restore publication headroom"* renders under `### Security`. The title only names a doc file (`DEVELOPMENT_DEPENDENCY_SECURITY.md`). Its sibling task with the same type and tags, without the word, correctly renders under `### Other`.

## Expected

A title keyword never outranks the strong tier. `Security` and `Deprecated` should come from type or tags first. The title should be consulted only after the strong-tier categories and the bug-like type default, as the function's own comment and the existing `Fixed`/`Changed` handling already do for other categories.

## Minimal repro

```ts
classifyItem({ type: "Task", tags: ["release"], title: "Exclude the dependency-security doc from the tarball", status: "closed" }, context)
// -> "Security"; expected "Other"
classifyItem({ type: "Task", tags: ["security"], title: "Rotate the signing key", status: "closed" }, context)
// -> "Security" (correct, strong tier)
```

## Suggested fix

Evaluate `security|cve|vulnerability` and `deprecated|deprecation` against `strongValues` first, then fall back to the sanitized title in the same weak-tier position as the other title-only checks. Add a regression test that pairs a title-only mention with a strong-tier non-security signal, and keep a negative control showing that an explicit `security` tag still wins.
classifyItem lets a title keyword (security, deprecated) outrank type and tags, so a title that names a doc file misfiles the entry under Security
